NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE (VIOLATION OF INSTRUCTIONS)
PROCEDURE, 2002
NORTH-WEST
FRONTIER PROVINCE
(VIOLATION OF
INSTRUCTIONS) PROCEDURE, 2002
[Gazette of
N.-W.F.P., Extraordinary Part I, 22nd August, 2002]
No. ROL/1 l-17/Power/2001,
dated 26-7-2002.---In pursuance of the provisions contained in clause (b)
of subsection (I) of section 38 of the Regulation of Generation. Transmission
and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997 (Act No. XL of 1997) the
Government of the North-West Frontier Province is pleased to make the following
Order to establish procedures for the purposes of the aforesaid provisions,
namely:--
1. Short title and
commencement. ---The procedure may be called the North-West Frontier
Province (Violation of Instructions) Procedure, 2002.
(2) These shall come into force
at once.
2. Definition.---In this Procedure,
unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context:
(i)
"Act" means the Regulation of Generation, Transmission and
Distribution of Electric Power Act (Act No. XL of 1997);
(ii)
"Code" means the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908;
(iii) "Electric
Inspector" means any person appointed under section 36 of Electricity Act,
1910;
(iv)
"Government" means the Government of the North-West Frontier
Province;
(v)
"Personal Assistant" means any official in the office of Electric
Inspector and so designated by the Electric Inspector to officially-record the
proceedings and maintenance of complaint register in the office of Inspection;
(vi)
"Presiding Officer" means the Electric Inspector;
(vii)
"Register of Complaints" means register to be maintained by the
Office of Inspector/subordinate office for the record of complaints;
(viii)
"Office of Inspector" means office of the Electric Inspector
appointed;
(ix)
"Subordinate office" means any subordinate office of an officer
appointed to assist the Electric Inspector/Presiding Officer, and holding a
post in BPS-16 or above;
(x)
"violation" means any act or omission contrary to any of the
provisions of the- Act and rules or Bye-laws, if any, made thereunder; and
(xi)
"Violator" means anyone who has committed a violation.
(2) Words not defined in this
Procedure shall have the same meanings as are assigned to them in the Act and
the Licensing (Distribution) Rules, 1999.
3. Filing of applications.---(1)
An aggrieved person, consumer or a licensee shall file separate petition for
each violation which shall contain full name and address of the petitioner, the
grounds giving rise to the violation and the name and address of the violator.
(2) The petition, duly signed by
the petitioner or his authorized representative, shall be supported by a
summary of evidence giving brief facts/data and arty documentary evidence,
alongwith such number of postal envelopes bearing postal stamps as may, from
time to time, be determined by the Presiding Officer, and the statements, facts
or opinion of the petitioner shall be verified by an affidavit.
(3) The petition shall--
(a) be filed
with such number of copies as the Presiding Officer may, from time to time,
determine and each set of the petition shall be completed in all respect;
(b) be ledged
during office hours at the office of Inspection or at subordinate office, as
the Presiding Officer may, from time to time, direct.
(4) All proceedings on a petition
shall be held at the Office of Inspection, unless the Presiding Officer
designates a different location preferably subordinate office in the notice.
(5) Personal Assistant or the
incharge of the subordinate office, as the case may be, shall examine the
contents of the petition to satisfy himself of the conformity thereof with the
procedure mentioned above.
(6) In case the petition is not
in accordance with the procedure aforementioned, the Personal Assistant or the
incharge of the subordinate office, as the case may be, shall return the
petition to the petitioner within three days of filing thereof with the
direction to refile the petition in compliance with laid down procedure:
p
sections.punishment:
punishable with a fine which may extend to ten thousand
rupees for each violation, and in case of continuous violation with a further
fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for every day during which the
violation has continued.
